The NoETL resource model: what a playbook costs in time, worker slots, memory, fuel and tool calls, with every figure labelled. The same file is published at `noetl.ai/dsl/resource-model.json`. Chapter 21 explains how to use it.

Model version **1**, figures as of **2026-11-11**. Purpose: Plan a playbook's time, slots, fuel, memory and tool calls before running it, then measure the run and refine.

```admonish warning title="Read this first"
- Latency on NoETL is dominated by orchestration per step, not by the work a step does. Count steps and sub-playbook hops before estimating anything else.
- Measurements are dated and environment-specific. A figure from kind does not transfer to prod, and an older figure may predate a fix.
- Live values beat this file: a running server answers /api/dsl/version; a running worker's limits are its env; actual cost is in the events and metrics listed under metrics.
```

## Labels

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **DEFAULT** | a code default (env var + value); a deployment may override it |
| **DEPLOYED** | read off the production cluster on as_of; configuration, not code |
| **GUIDANCE** | a planning rule derived from the figures; not a measurement |
| **MEASURED** | observed on a cluster or harness; read environment/date/source before reusing it |
| **NOT_YET_MEASURED** | a real question with no number; do not invent one |
| **TARGET** | a goal or budget; not a measurement |

### routing

- **label**: DEFAULT
- **source**: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/worker.rs:233-244
- **text**: A worker claims only its pool's subject (commands.<pool>.>); a step reaches a pool through the pool its command is published to. Orchestration of system/* drives runs on the system pool.

### slot_model

- **label**: DEFAULT
- **source**: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/worker.rs:313, 748-754
- **text**: A worker process has WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENT slots (a semaphore). A slot is acquired before the worker pulls a command and released when that command's tool returns. A pool's capacity is replicas x slots; commands beyond it queue on the command bus.

## Heuristics

| Label | Source | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| GUIDANCE |  | Estimate wall clock as steps x per_step_overhead + sum(step work) + hops x hop_overhead, where hops are kind: playbook children. On prod today use ~4.5 s per step and ~9-15 s per hop (orchestration_overhead.measured), and re-measure: the overhead, not the work, decides the total. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Prefer an inline python step to a kind: playbook child when the child only wraps one call: each hop measured ~9-15 s of orchestration on prod, and inlining cut a planner turn by 44%. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Count slots, not steps, for concurrency: a parallel loop dispatches every item at once and max_in_flight does not throttle it, so N items need N free slots on the target pool or the rest queue. The prod user pool has 8 slots at minimum and 80 at maximum; the system pool has 4. |
| GUIDANCE |  | An awaited child (return_result / return_step) or a hosted agent's playbook tool holds the parent's slot while the child needs another. Budget two slots per awaiting parent and avoid sending both to a small pool. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Bound every loop and back-edge with a when: guard on an explicit counter: the server enforces no iteration cap, and each pass is a full step. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Set timeout_seconds on python, shell, postgres, duckdb and rhai steps that call anything slow: those kinds have no default timeout and the worker has no per-command one. |
| GUIDANCE |  | For kind: wasm, plan inside the defaults (30 s, 10e9 fuel, 1024 MiB) and expect one module at a time per worker process: concurrent wasm steps on one pod serialize. Read fuel actually spent from the worker's debug log; no metric reports it. |
| GUIDANCE |  | For kind: agent, the tool-call budget (32) and child timeout (180 s) bound a hosted loop: worst case is about 32 x 180 s = 96 min of one held slot. Size max_turns and the tool list so the expected path uses a few calls, and read agent.final for the real count. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Keep step results under 100 KiB when a downstream step reads them: larger results are spilled to the result store and every read becomes a fetch. |
| GUIDANCE |  | Choose a pool by where the work must run (credentials, network, memory) first; then check its slot capacity against the plan's peak parallelism. Bursts above capacity on the user pool trigger KEDA scale-up, which can add node provisioning time (~60-90 s) on Autopilot. |
| TARGET | noetl/server orchestrate-core dsl-manifest worker_runtime.agent.playbook_tools.not_durable | Orchestrator-driven resume of a hosted agent loop after a worker dies (today the step restarts from turn 1). |

## Metrics

- **events_note**: agent.* events come only from the hosted loop (NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_PLAYBOOK_TOOLS=true). Token usage is in call.done result data, not on agent.* events.
- **server_prometheus_source**: noetl/server src/metrics.rs, served at GET /metrics
- **worker_prometheus_source**: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/metrics.rs, served on WORKER_METRICS_BIND, else 0.0.0.0:$PORT, else 0.0.0.0:9090

### apis

- returns: started_at, completed_at and up to 2000 most recent events with created_at; no duration field (subtract); route: GET /api/executions/{id}
- returns: progress step counts only, no times; route: GET /api/executions/{id}/status

### events

- fields: result.context: status, duration_ms, error, exit_code, child_execution_id; an agent step's result data carries usage {input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens}, turns, model, stop_reason; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/command.rs:1097-1110; noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/result.rs:62-135, src/tools/agent.rs:838-851; type: call.done
- fields: created_at on each event: the difference is the step's wall clock including slot wait after claim; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/command.rs:545-557, 1352-1361; type: command.started / command.completed / command.failed
- fields: turn, outcome (tool_calls \| final), tool_calls \[{id, name}\]; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/agent_host.rs:226-254; type: agent.turn
- fields: turn, tool_use_id, tool, binding, playbook, child_execution_id, is_error, duration_ms, input and result previews (2 KiB); source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/agent_host.rs:307-321; type: agent.tool_call
- fields: turns, tool_calls, child_execution_ids, duration_ms; or refused: tool_call_budget; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/agent_host.rs:231-240, 259-262; type: agent.final

### not_available

- no per-execution or per-step duration histogram on the server
- no metric for wasm fuel consumed (debug log only)
- no metric for token usage (call.done result data only)
- no per-tool memory metric

### server_prometheus

- labels: event_type; name: noetl_event_ingest_duration_seconds; type: histogram
- labels: phase; meaning: where inside event ingest the time goes; name: noetl_event_ingest_phase_seconds; type: histogram
- name: noetl_orchestrate_in_flight_executions / noetl_orchestrate_oldest_seconds; type: gauge
- labels: entry, outcome; name: noetl_execute_outcomes_total; type: counter

### worker_prometheus

- labels: tool_kind; meaning: full dispatch per command: tool + case evaluation + lifecycle emits; buckets 0.01-120 s; name: noetl_worker_dispatch_duration_seconds; type: histogram
- meaning: slots in use on this worker; name: noetl_worker_concurrent_dispatches; type: gauge
- labels: phase (park \| outcome); meaning: claim latency split; name: noetl_worker_command_pickup_phase_seconds; type: histogram
- labels: event_type; name: noetl_worker_event_emit_duration_seconds; type: histogram
- labels: phase (fetch \| compile); meaning: wasm cold start; name: noetl_worker_plugin_load_seconds; type: histogram
- labels: limit (fuel \| timeout \| memory); name: noetl_worker_plugin_limit_trips_total; type: counter
- meaning: cost of spilling an over-budget result; name: noetl_worker_result_store_put_duration_seconds; type: histogram
- labels: version; meaning: which worker build answered; absence of a newer metric means that build predates it; name: noetl_worker_build_info; type: gauge

## Orchestration overhead

- **caveat**: Per-step cost varies with load and with the server build: several of these figures predate later dispatch fixes. Measure on the target cluster at the target load before committing to a budget.
- **summary**: Each step pays a fixed orchestration cost (command dispatch, claim, and three lifecycle event emits) on top of its work; each kind: playbook hop pays a whole child execution's worth.
